One Grammar for Code, Data, Markup and Queries: Closing the Agent Operational Circle

2026-09-06Autonomous Systems & Grammar6 min read

These notes were written in September 2026, before the C host was removed, and describe designs as well as shipped behaviour. Where a post says asl-host check or asl-host test, the command today is asl check or asl test; ERR_READ_UNBALANCED is now ERR_UNBALANCED; and the current checker does not reject an unmarked effect (ERR_EFFECT_UNMARKED). Figures are the ones measured on the date each post gives. Current docs

By GenSEAM | September 2026

AgentSlang (ASL) gives coding agents a single S-expression notation across their entire loop: program modules, configuration ledgers, batched tool calls, HTML/SVG views and SQL queries are all written as balanced forms and checked before they run. Renderers in the standard packages turn those checked forms into the SQL dialect, HTML5/SVG markup or shell invocation the outside world expects.

Compare that with the Tower of Babel inside a typical agent's context window. During a single task, a model is asked to juggle incompatible syntaxes and escaping rules at once:

  1. Configuration: JSON (comma drift, quote escaping) and YAML (indentation traps).
  2. Visual Output & Markup: raw SVG XML and HTML, with verbose closing tags and unescaped attributes.
  3. Command Execution: raw Bash strings, where nested quotes and $() expansions trigger silent failures or injection.
  4. Data Querying: hand-concatenated SQL across PostgreSQL, SQLite, MySQL and ClickHouse.

Closing The Agent Operational Circle removes those syntax switches by letting the model author one checked notation everywhere. (The claim of this post is architectural; we have not measured what share of task failures multi-syntax switching accounts for.)

1. The Four Quadrants of Autonomous Operation

The design goal: the agent does not write raw JSON, YAML, SVG, HTML or Bash. It writes AgentSlang Notation (ASN), and renderers produce the external format.

Universal ASN S-expression
├── Quadrant 1: shell and execution (:sh)        → quoted POSIX sh
├── Quadrant 2: vector visuals and UI (:svg :vdom) → SVG XML
├── Quadrant 3: schema and data (:config :wire)  → JSON and YAML
└── Quadrant 4: relational querying (asl-sql)    → Postgres, SQLite, MySQL, ClickHouse

Every quadrant shares the same syntactic rules:

  • One Delimiter Rule: every expression is enclosed in balanced (...), and an unbalanced form is caught by a balance check (asl '(:check :file "...")') before anything evaluates it.
  • Short Keywords: attributes and verbs are short keywords (:cmd, :args, :rc, :circ, :f, :s).
  • Rendering as Library Code: the renderers are ASL functions in the repository, listed per quadrant below with their test status on 2026-10-14.

2. Quadrant 1: Structured Shell Execution (:sh)

The Fragility of Shell Strings

Prompting an LLM to generate bash -c "..." invites trouble. A command like:

find packages -name "*.asl" -exec grep -l "TODO" {} + | xargs wc -l

is exposed to unescaped quotes, glob misinterpretation, BSD (macOS) versus GNU (Linux) differences, and pipelines that fail silently without set -eo pipefail.

The ASN Form

In ASN, a command is data with an explicit argument vector:

(:sh :pipe
  (:cmd "find" :args ["packages" "-name" "*.asl"])
  (:cmd "wc" :args ["-l"]))

This form is not shorter: tiktoken 0.12.0 counts 34 tokens for it against 12 for the equivalent find packages -name "*.asl" | wc -l (both o200k_base and cl100k_base, 2026-09-24). What it buys is that every argument is a separate string, so quoting is the renderer's job, not the model's.

What exists today:

  1. asl/packages/asl-target-sh/src/emitSh.asl prints POSIX sh with single-quote quarantine: a literal it's safe becomes 'it'\''s safe', $(rm -rf /) becomes '$(rm -rf /)', and a variable becomes "${user_input:-}". Its suite asl/packages/asl-target-sh/tests/emitShTest.asl passes (asl test: 12 assertions, 1 refutation).
  2. asl/packages/asl-transpile/src/shTranspile.asl (asnToSh, shToAsn) converts between the :sh form and script text; its suite passes with 22 assertions.

Executing an argument vector directly through execve, with no shell in between, is the direction we are building toward; today the output is a script.

3. Quadrant 2: Vector Graphics and Visual Output (:svg)

The SVG XML Token Tax

When generating icons, UI cards or diagrams, raw XML repeats attribute names on every element (x1="...", y1="...", stroke-width="..."), and on large drawings a capped generation can end mid-element.

The ASN Form

(:svg :w 400 :h 400
  (:circ :cx 200 :cy 180 :r 80 :f "#ff00cc")
  (:rc :x 120 :y 140 :w 160 :h 5 :f "#050510")
  (:rc :x 120 :y 150 :w 160 :h 8 :f "#050510")
  (:ln :x1 0 :y1 300 :x2 400 :y2 300 :s "#00ffff" :sw 2)
  (:ln :x1 200 :y1 300 :x2 200 :y2 400 :s "#00ffff" :sw 2))

This drawing costs 151 tokens against 172 for its hand-written SVG equivalent on o200k_base (12.2 percent fewer; 151 against 171 on cl100k_base). Two renderers turn it into SVG: asl/packages/asl-vdom/src/asnSvg.asl and asl/packages/asl-transpile/src/svgTranspile.asl; their suites pass (asnSvgTest 27 assertions, svgTranspileTest 62). The SVG they emit can then be rasterized by standard tools such as resvg or librsvg. Why LLMs Choke on SVG XML has the details.

4. Quadrant 3: Configuration & Wire Frames (:wire)

Why write JSON or YAML when you can write ASN?

  • JSON overhead: quoted keys, commas, braces and colons.
  • YAML drift: indentation bugs that change the tree.

ASN writes configuration and inter-agent frames as keywords and values:

(:wire :msgId "w-901" :op :taskPropose
  :target "worker-4"
  :payload (:task "runGate" :strict true :timeoutMs 10000))

This frame costs 44 tokens against 52 for the same record as JSON (json.dumps with default separators), on both o200k_base and cl100k_base: 15 percent fewer. Converters exist in asl/packages/asl-transpile/src/transpile.asl (jsonToAsn, asnToJson, yamlToAsn, asnToYaml); its suite passes with 81 assertions, and the YAML converter's own suite with 42.

5. Measured Across the Circle

The three examples in this post, counted with tiktoken 0.12.0 on 2026-09-24 over the exact text shown (ASN form against the external form):

ExampleExternal FormatASN (o200k)External (o200k)Change
Shell pipeline (section 2)Bash string3412ASN costs 22 more
Vector drawing (section 3)SVG XML15117212.2% fewer
Wire frame (section 4)JSON445215.4% fewer

Three hand-picked examples are not a benchmark, and we have not measured failure rates for either form. They show the trade: ASN is cheaper where the external format repeats keys and closing tags, dearer where the external format is terse, and structurally uniform everywhere.

6. Closing the Loop

Autonomous agents should not have to be interpreters for a stack of human-oriented serialization formats.

By writing data, markup, visuals and commands in one S-expression notation, the model spends its capacity on the task instead of on each format's escaping rules, and the renderers carry those rules once, in code that can be tested.
